content_units: Best First Binge for Your Taste

You’ll likely enjoy   Only Murders in the Building   first, with   Severance   as the stronger second pick if you want something darker and more suspenseful. Based on your priorities—  character writing, mystery, humor  , and avoiding   excessive violence   or stories that get   too convoluted  —the best choices are the ones that stay clever without becoming punishing to track.
Ranked Watch Order
Rank   Show   Why it fits you   Violence level   Complexity
1     Only Murders in the Building     Strong mystery hook, charming character chemistry, light humor, easy to follow   Low   Low-Medium
2     Severance     Excellent character writing, gripping mystery, darkly funny, very compelling   Low-Medium   Medium
3     The Good Place     Smart, funny, warm, character-driven, very bingeable   Very low   Low-Medium
4     Fleabag     Brilliant character writing and sharp humor, but less of a mystery show   Low   Low
5     Dark     Outstanding mystery ambition, but likely too complex for your stated preference   Medium   High
Option 1:   Only Murders in the Building     Best overall fit: witty mystery with lovable leads and low barrier to entry     Top match
-   Pros:   Fun central mystery, strong ensemble chemistry, consistently funny, stylish but easy to watch.
-   Cons:   Less emotionally deep than the very best prestige dramas; mystery stakes stay relatively cozy.
-   Best for:   Viewers who want a binge that is clever, character-friendly, and entertaining without stress.
View series
Option 2:   Severance     Best if you want a more serious mystery with exceptional atmosphere and character work     Best darker pick
-   Pros:   Outstanding concept, sharp writing, fascinating mystery, dry humor, memorable characters.
-   Cons:   Slower burn; unanswered questions build over time.
-   Best for:   Viewers who enjoy puzzling intrigue as long as it remains emotionally grounded.
View series
Option 3:   The Good Place     Best comfort binge: funny, inventive, and surprisingly thoughtful     Safest pick
-   Pros:   Great character arcs, fast episodes, lots of humor, very low violence, easy to follow.
-   Cons:   Mystery element is lighter than in your top-interest shows.
-   Best for:   Anyone wanting heart, humor, and smart writing over suspense.
View series
Option 4:   Fleabag     Best pure writing showcase, but not the strongest match for your mystery preference     Writing-first choice
-   Pros:   Elite character writing, hilarious and emotionally sharp, very bingeable.
-   Cons:   Not really a mystery series; more intimate and character-focused than plot-driven.
-   Best for:   Viewers who want brilliant voice, emotional complexity, and dark comedy.
View series
Option 5:   Dark     Best for puzzle-box lovers, but the riskiest fit for you     High complexity
-   Pros:   Deep mystery, ambitious plotting, strong atmosphere, rewarding if you like untangling details.
-   Cons:   Can become difficult to track; heavier tone; more intense than your ideal balance suggests.
-   Best for:   Viewers who actively enjoy dense timelines, constant theory-building, and high complexity.
View series
Why This Ranking Fits Your Preferences
Your ideal first binge is probably:
-   Character-driven enough   to keep you attached
-   Mystery-forward   without requiring a wall chart
-   Funny enough   to avoid feeling grim
-   Low in violence   and not emotionally exhausting
That makes   Only Murders in the Building   the cleanest match. It hits all three of your positives at once—character writing, mystery, humor—while avoiding both of your negatives.
Severance   is a very close runner-up if you want something more intense and prestige-drama styled. It’s more mysterious and arguably richer than Only Murders, but also more withholding and slower.
Dark   is the one I would specifically  not  recommend as your first binge, even though it is excellent, because “impossible to follow” is exactly the risk with it.
Best Starting Picks by Mood
-   Want the best all-around first binge:     Only Murders in the Building
-   Want the strongest mystery with great writing:     Severance
-   Want the funniest, easiest binge:     The Good Place
-   Want the best pure character writing:     Fleabag
-   Want the most ambitious puzzle-box story:     Dark
Quick Actions
Start with Only Murders
Try Severance instead
